title: ARPG I’ve been building for the past 10 months
author: Alstroph

comments.author: Alstroph
comments.body: The software engineering was done with Claude Code, for the graphics I use Flux 2 Text to Image and Image to Image, Meshy for 3D models, and some editor workflows to decimate meshes, fit armor, etc. The dungeon theme was hand written, but the town theme is Suno, that will be replaced with a hand written song in the near future.

replies.body: Nice, and I must ask. How much was spent on tokens in total or I guess how much in total was it for the pass 10 months cause this is incredible work!

replies.author: Alstroph
replies.body: Thanks! I’m approaching 800 hours of time invested, Claude Max. I’m not sure many tokens, but obscene amounts for sure.

comments.author: vexmach1ne
comments.body: Cool diabloesque game! I don't think you'll get much traction unfortunately due to who you're competing against but kudos to you for sticking to it this far. I bet it was loads of fun and you learned so mich! I hope you prove me wrong!

replies.author: Alstroph
replies.body: Yeah there are some titans I’m up against, but I’m hoping to grab a different crowd with this one. Diablo II was excellent, but it lost some of the slow, tactical hardcore dread that made Diablo 1 great. So I aim for this to be more of a branch off of Diablo 1 instead. I hope there are some out there that are looking for the same, I know I am. Grim Dawn and POE 2 were the closest, but not quite what I am looking for.

replies.author: theflossboss1
replies.body: Not to demoralize but you are also competing against all the other AI driven game devs who are building a similar game as well

replies.author: Alstroph
replies.body: For sure, but it’ll take them 800+ hours too!

replies.author: IsThisASnakeInMyBoot
replies.body:
If you're going for slow and tactical that's not what I got from this clip at all. It looks extremely fast paced like the speed at which you're sprinting through environments is kinda silly, and it kinda looks like you just walk up and bash things til they fall over. I like the vision, and the game does look interesting but try and get those things to connect. Even the walking in dungeons seems pretty slow.

As a suggestion, maybe lower the walking/running speeds til it feels a little more weighted, and then have a mount system outside of dungeons. It'll achieve that same thing you're going for I think. Also would be worth changing the font of the character's name so it fits in with the aesthetic a bit more

comments.author: Acceptable_Movie6712
comments.body:
It’s always fascinating watching people develop full games with ai. It just doesn’t really make sense to use it for anything other than a prototype. Like, doing this teaches you nothing and you end up with a lesser version of what you’re emulating. 

Kind of like the guy making counter strike but with paintballs. Like, if you’re curious if a game idea will work, ai dev makes sense, otherwise it’s just very odd.

replies.author: Alstroph
replies.body: I’ve been a professional software engineer for over 10 years and I’ve been making games as a hobby since I was 13. AI assisted engineering is an addition to my tool belt, but not a crutch.

replies.author: Acceptable_Movie6712
replies.body: Nice I have a similar background. it’s fascinating stuff for sure. AI definitely can help produce whatever people want it to do, sadly it can’t help define if something’s even worth doing at all.

replies.author: Alstroph
replies.body: As long as you have fun it’s worth it right? I have realistic expectations for this, I expect to make $0, which is why I made sure to host the alpha servers and site for as cheap as possible (I’d have to double check AWS and cloudflare but I think I’m at $0 hosting cost still)

replies.author: Acceptable_Movie6712
replies.body: Honestly, yeah if you’re not delusional about it then for sure. It’s pretty sick to see your vision come to life. Who cares what a stick in the mud like me thinks? Rock on 🤘

replies.body: I disagree. Fail fast, learn fast.  How long would it have taken him to solo dev a game like this to this point? Surely more than 800 hours from knowing nothing. Now people can see the work and criticize it. He can internalize that and make it better at a much faster pace than a non-AI assisted dev.

replies.author: Acceptable_Movie6712
replies.body: I mean that’s literally what I’m saying lol. I’m not sure how developing an entire game is “failing fast and learning fast” compared to rendering multiple prototypes.

replies.author: teamharder
replies.body: Trying to take my games beyond prototypes taught me much more than the initial goofing around that I did. Just my experience.

comments.author: zreakz
comments.body:
This looks really good. I am still waiting to see a full-ai game that has actual effort put into it and this looks like one of the best so far.

Can you elaborate a bit more on your workflows to get armor to fit and how you created the graphics for the terrain? (Such as the cave walls)

replies.author: Alstroph
replies.body:
I used Flux 2 to make the textures, and I created a map editor to work on the town, most of that is hand placed. 

The armor fitting is very difficult, I made a python based asset pipeline. I used flux 2 to generate the base player model, then with flux 2 img to img i can add armor to that player model, then with a second prompt i can remove the player model so that only the armor remains. This has helped a lot with proportions. Then I bake the skin weights onto the armor pieces and inflate the mesh out a bit for clearance. 

The base player model is sliced so that regions can be hidden, such as the torso. For boots, the foot is completely hidden

replies.author: zreakz
replies.body: Very good idea with the armor workflow, appreciate you sharing!

comments.author: Charming-Author4877
comments.body:
I really don't want to sound negative, just what is the intention; where you are heading?  
The visuals are very outdated, the gameplay looks like bare minimum.  
Your demo/trailer does not showcase anything that would raise interest.

I believe barebones visuals can work out, though your game appears to try hard to not be like that and it's not working out.  
Those type of games, they live from a few core principles - addictive improvement and bigger and bigger slaughters. So you progress from weak to being a "god".  
And these days they are also centered around social collaboration.  
Pure single player needs very deep and smart lore or amazing game design.

replies.author: Alstroph
replies.body:
I’m aiming for fans of late 90’s and early 2000 ARPGs here. Also, this is a multiplayer only game, server authority.

I do have a very deep end game in development, but I don’t want to spoil it at this time.

replies.body: Wish you the best, hope it works out that way. Sounds more promising than the trailer looked like

comments.author: albertyto
comments.body:
From my experience, the issue is always the art. Even if you've good mechanics/systems, when the art sucks or doesn't click, then it is a mesh.

In my case, I created a prototype with a generative pipeline, till the state where I like how the concept performs, but the gameplay sucks, not because of the systems but because of the art. I decided that learning low poly with Blender + VFX in Godot would yield better result on the "feel" part than expending more time on generative AI for art.
